transcript:
This message comes from Schwab. At Schwab, you can get everything from self-directed investing to full-service wealth management, all in one place.
No matter your investing goal, life stage, amount to invest, or know-how, you can invest your way with Schwab.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. Tennessee Governor Bob Lee has halted executions from being carried out in the state
after a death row inmate survived two doses of a lethal injection drug.
In a statement, Lee said he is also ordering an outside investigation.
Katherine Sweeney is a reporter with member station WPLN. She was among the media witnesses who described what they saw to other reporters.
This is an enormous dose of a sedative. That should not ever need to happen twice, but it did, and then she stayed alive.
I think one of the issues we have here is the protocol doesn't talk about what happens if you do this twice and they're still alive.
I don't think that that is something that was planned for.
A statement from the state corrections department says Christa Gail Pike has been transported to an offsite medical facility.
She had been sentenced to death for a 1995 murder when she was 18.
Against the backdrop of the war with Iran, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Wednesday, delivered what he called a state of the force address at a military base in Virginia.
Hegseth announced some major changes, including slashing the number of generals and admirals by 20 percent. Here's NPR's Tom Bowman.
He's also fired a number of senior black and female officers questioning whether they got the job because of their race or gender.
Also, the top Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee, Jack Reed, said lawmakers have a role here and Hegseth must come to Capitol Hill to explain his reasoning for these cuts.
Hegseth's speech came on the same day that U.S. forces formally withdrew from Iraq after more than two decades.
Iran says it has received an official U.S. response to Tehran's proposal to bring an end to the seven-month war.
Foreign Minister Abbas Araxi presented the response at a Cabinet meeting Wednesday.
President Trump rejected the latest offer a few days ago, but Araxi has said that Iran has not received a formal rejection.
President Trump announced that South Korea will invest $200 billion in energy projects in the U.S.
and Piers Anthony Kuhn reports from Seoul that it's part of a $350 billion investment deal that South Korea agreed to last year in exchange for lower U.S. tariffs.
The projects include a gas-fired power plant in Texas, eight large nuclear power plants in several states, and investment in a natural gas pipeline in Alaska.
President Trump called the projects a major step toward securing the U.S.'s energy supply chain.
The announcement's timing is widely seen as a bid to burnish Trump's economic record ahead of midterm elections.
South Korea's Ministry of Industry, though, says in a statement that there's been no decision on whether or how much South Korea will invest in the Alaska pipeline.
A U.S. Commerce Department fact sheet says that whether work on the project goes ahead depends on whether it's considered commercially viable.
Anthony Kuhn, NPR News, Seoul.
Many overseas and military voters use two absentee voting forms that are overseen by the Pentagon.
In August, the Trump administration made an emergency request to remove a long-standing category for U.S. citizens who are born abroad and have never lived in the United States.
And sometimes because their U.S. citizen parents or legal guardians served overseas in the U.S. military.
Many states allow these citizens to vote if a parent last lived or was registered to vote there before leaving the country.
The Pentagon says it now believes those overseas citizens are not eligible to use its forms.
But that state election officials can continue processing older versions of the forms.
The change comes after the Republican National Committee sued more than a half a dozen states for allowing these U.S. citizens to vote.
Kansi Luang, NPR News.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announces 20 percent cut to generals and admirals at military base
Defense Secretary Hegseth fires senior black and female officers questioning whether they got jobs based on race or gender
U.S. forces formally withdraw from Iraq after more than two decades of military presence
Iran receives official U.S. response to Tehran's proposal to end seven-month war with Iran
South Korea to invest $200 billion in U.S. energy projects including nuclear plants and gas pipeline
Trump administration removes citizenship category from Pentagon absentee voting forms for overseas-born U.S. citizens
